name: Cologix Santa Clara SV1 Data Center

profile.reading: Cologix is a network-neutral interconnection and edge data center operator headquartered in Denver, Colorado, operational since December 2010, describing itself as North America's leading network-neutral interconnection and hyperscale edge data center company, with more than 45 facilities across 13 North American markets serving roughly 2,000 customers with access to more than 725 networks and more than 350 cloud service providers, per the operator's own materials. This facility, SV1, sits at 2050 Martin Avenue, Santa Clara, California 95050, per the operator's own current data centers listing page, which describes SV1 as the company's Silicon Valley hub for modern workloads; an independent reverse geocode of this record's own stored coordinates returned a closely matching, same-block address (2040 Martin Avenue) at maximum confidence, a ten-number difference consistent with an adjacent building on the same short block rather than a mismatch, corroborating the operator's own published address. Cologix acquired this Silicon Valley facility from vXchnge in the company's 2020-2021 acquisition wave, part of a broader growth pattern of acquisitions beginning in 2010 that also included Navisite, The Minnesota Gateway, Canix, MetroOptic in 2019, and Cyxtera in 2023 (the last of which connects to the separate Cyxtera operator record tracked elsewhere in this registry). No square footage, MW capacity, or year-opened figure specific to SV1 was located in sourcing reachable this session; the operator's own SV1 page did not publish these figures in the materials reached this session, consistent with Cologix's general practice across several of its smaller edge facilities of publishing marketing copy without detailed technical specification sheets. Santa Clara's Martin Avenue corridor sits within the broader Silicon Valley data center cluster that also hosts CoreSite, Digital Realty, and other operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, drawing on the area's dense fiber routes and proximity to major cloud and enterprise customers headquartered in the South Bay.

reading.body:
Cologix SV1 in Santa Clara publishes no power capacity, no square footage, and no year opened. The facility sits on Martin Avenue in Silicon Valley's dense fiber corridor alongside other major operators, acquired by Cologix from vXchnge in 2020-2021 as part of the company's broader growth through acquisition across thirteen North American markets. The operator describes it as a hub for modern workloads but does not publish the technical specifications needed to measure its scale in compute terms.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities of which only eleven publish power capacity totaling 365 MW. SV1 does not appear among those eleven published figures, placing it in the 92 unmeasured facilities that make up the state's actual capacity. Without a published power envelope, SV1 cannot be ranked among California's largest by compute potential, though the state context ranks it twelfth among published capacity—a ranking that reflects the absence of data rather than a measured position.

SV1's relevance to AI infrastructure depends entirely on specifications Cologix has not published. The Silicon Valley location and network-neutral model suggest it could host cloud and enterprise workloads including AI, but power capacity, cooling architecture, and existing tenant density remain opaque. To assess whether this campus matters to AI scaling, a reader would need to contact the operator directly.
